newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen weak at opening.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen weak at opening.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open lower Monday at the start of a week dominated by economic data and Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Congressional testimony Wednesday.

"A lot of numbers are coming in. The market will be colored by that, and we have Greenspan coming up," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "The mood is cautious. We've had three days on the downside." Data today include January personal income and consumption ahead of the bell and February purchasing agents at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
This week's key piece of data, the February employment report, is due out on Friday.
Westfalia Investments director of research Peter Cardillo said that the Dow's consolidation was not yet over.

"We still have 250 points on the downside before the market begins to stabilize," Cardillo said. "That doesn't mean it will happen all at once. It will be a gradual decline throughout March and April.
"We have a slew of reports due out. I think we'll see choppy trading ahead of the February employment report this Friday," he said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average lost 127.87 points, or 0.69 percent, to 18,429.13.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down 8.6 at 4299.7.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, Schlumberger Ltd was down 1/2 at 100-1/8 and Baker Hughes Inc was down 3/8 at 35-1/8. Coca-Cola Co was down 3/8 at 60-5/8. Philip Morris Cos Inc shares were up 1/4 at 135-3/8.
The dollar was firm in Tokyo, steady in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly lower, with the long bond down 11/32 to yield 6.83 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that Ford Motor Co is likely to be disappointed if it expects its planned public offering of Hertz shares to provide a quick boost to Ford's own lackluster market valuation.
